A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same portable visuo-tactile gripper and learning framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original real-robot results on four manipulation tasks, tactile reconstruction results, pretraining ablations and failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds sensor-replacement and task-exclusion experiments in Appendices A and B.2.

M1.justification: The sensor design, masked tactile reconstruction, CLIP-based visual encoder, cross-attention fusion and diffusion policy remain unchanged. Condensed equations and explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds Test Tube Collection evaluation with newly fabricated tactile sensors, extending the tested sensor conditions. The base pretraining corpus and four downstream manipulation tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Vision-Only, Ours w/o Cross-Attention and Ours w/o Pretraining as comparators. The new appendix comparisons vary sensors or pretraining data for the same algorithm rather than introduce another comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 adds sensor-replacement reevaluation and two protocols excluding the corresponding downstream task from pretraining, followed by encoder retraining and policy fine-tuning. The original four-task protocol remains 20 trials per task with policies trained for 60 epochs.

E4.justification: Appendices A and B.2 add focused checks of sensor interchangeability and dependence on same-task pretraining demonstrations. Existing dataset-size, demonstration-count, epoch, attention and failure analyses are retained, with some moved into the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the seed-42 pretraining configuration and report point success rates without multi-seed summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new comparisons do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 scores and plotted results are unchanged. New Table 2 reports 0.85 whole-task success with both original and replacement sensors. Table 3 reports 0.80 versus 0.85 for Test Tube Collection and 0.75 versus 0.70 for Whiteboard Erasing when corresponding task demonstrations are excluded versus retained in pretraining; these are new controlled-condition comparisons.

T1.justification: v1's explicit masking equation is omitted, but the same masking operation remains described. Reconstruction objectives, cross-attention and diffusion mathematics retain their meaning; no substantive assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: portable tactile hardware, cross-modal representation and policy learning, and the large-scale manipulation dataset. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new tests as evidence of sensor reliability and interchangeability, and of representation transfer without dependence on target-task pretraining examples. Existing mechanism explanations and the single-arm, parallel-gripper applicability boundary remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses that demonstration collection and robot deployment used different physical sensor pairs throughout the project. This clarifies existing hardware use rather than documenting a redesign. Hyperparameter tables, synchronization details and resource-access statements are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Sparsh and Transferable Tactile Transformers, with a brief discussion of pretraining across sensors and tasks. Existing positioning relative to 3D-ViTac, UMI and ViTaMIn is retained.

P1.justification: v2 condenses selected related-work, method and discussion passages, reorganizes appendix subsections, and moves dataset-size and downstream-attention discussions out of the main text. The main section sequence remains intact; venue and acknowledgments are also updated.

P2.justification: v2 adds two result tables, adjusts table styling and redistributes existing figures. v1 Figures 6 and 9 become appendix Figures 8 and 10, respectively. Existing plots and visual examples are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The new sensor-consistency and task-exclusion controls strengthen empirical support for portability and representation transfer while preserving the original evidence. The gain is limited: these are narrow additional checks, and the absence of uncertainty estimates limits conclusions from their near-equal success rates.
